The denominator is $3-\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $3+\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $3+\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\text{i}}{3-\text{i}} & =\frac{4\text{i}}{3-\text{i}}\cdot \frac{3+\text{i}}{3+\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{4\text{i}(3+\text{i})}{{3}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{12\text{i}+4{\text{i}}^{2}}{{3}^{2}-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{12\text{i}+4(-1)}{9+1} \\  & =\frac{-4+12\text{i}}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-4+12\text{i}}{10} & =-\frac{4}{10}+\frac{12}{10}\text{i} \\  & =-\frac{2}{5}+\frac{6}{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
